Here’s the consolidated 12-week plan summary (training, cardio, nutrition, recovery) starting Monday, 2026-06-01, tailored for a 31-year-old female with PCOS. Emphasis: resistance training first, glycaemic control, cautious HIIT use, phased nutrition for fat loss without under-fuelling.

Global guardrails
- Frequency: 3 full-body strength sessions/week; 2–3 cardio sessions/week (mostly Zone 2); optional 1 HIIT session/week, max 2/week if recovery is excellent.
- RPE: Main lifts RPE 6–8 (top sets up to 8.5 in Phase 2 push); accessories 6–8; avoid failure.
- Progression: Double progression (reps → load), smallest load jumps.
- Red flags to deload/trim: Resting HR up ≥7 bpm for 3 mornings, sleep <6 h, cravings up, mood volatility, or performance drops twice in a row.
- PCOS-specific: No fasted strength/HIIT; maintain carbs around training; use machine variations during PMS/bleed if energy low.

Weekly structure template
- Mon: Strength A
- Tue: Cardio (Zone 2 or HIIT per plan)
- Wed: Optional easy Zone 2 or rest + mobility
- Thu: Strength B
- Fri: Zone 2 (plus brief 10 s spin-ups if appropriate)
- Sat: Strength C
- Sun: Optional easy walk (NEAT)

Warm-up each strength day
- 5–8 min easy cardio + mobility (thoracic rotations, 90/90 hips, ankle rocks).
- 1–2 ramp-up sets per main lift.

Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3, Jun 1–21) – Foundation/insulin-sensitizing base
- Goal: Learn movements, moderate volume, RPE 6–7.
- Strength A (Mon):
  - Goblet squat 3x8–10
  - RDL 3x8
  - DB bench 3x8–10

- Add a small, strategic dose of HIIT 1–2 times per week, capped, and placed to protect lower-body strength days.
- Autoregulate by symptoms; if sleep, mood, or resting HR drift, HIIT is the first thing to pull back.

- Session cap: 12–20 total work intervals per week, across 1–2 sessions.
- Interval style: Short, alactic-to-glycolytic efforts with full or near-full recovery so lactate doesn’t accumulate excessively.
- Modalities: Bike, rower, uphill treadmill walk, or elliptical to minimize impact.
- Fueling: Small pre-HIIT carb + protein (15–25 g of each if not near a meal). Post-HIIT protein 20–30 g and a modest carb serving. Never do HIIT fasted.

A true 1RM test isn’t ideal here at the end of Phase 3. It adds high neural and joint stress, which can disrupt recovery, sleep, and cycle regularity—counterproductive for PCOS and for maintaining insulin sensitivity while in a fat-loss phase. You’ll get nearly the same insight with lower risk by using submax tests and estimated 1RM.

Recommended approach for Week 12 assessments
- Use rep-maxes at RPE 9- and estimate 1RM with Epley or RIR-based tables. Target:
  - Squat variant: 3–5RM @RPE 9- (stop one clean rep in reserve)
  - Hip thrust or RDL: 5RM @RPE 9-
  - DB bench or machine press: 6–8RM @RPE 9-
  - Pull (row or pulldown/assisted pull-up): 6–8RM @RPE 9-
- Estimation: e1RM = weight × (1 + reps/30) for sets of 3–10 reps. Track e1RM trend rather than a single-day max.

If you still want a single attempt day
- Do a controlled, low-risk “heavy single” approach at ≤RPE 8 (about 90–93% of true 1RM) to gauge readiness without grinding.
- Protocol (example for squat/hinge/press):
  1) General warm-up 5–8 min + movement prep
  2) Ramped sets of 3–5–3–2 reps to ~80–85%
  3) One to two singles at RPE 7.5–8 (bar speed stays snappy)
  4) Back-off set: 1 set of 3–5 reps at ~85% to confirm strength
- Stop if bar speed drops markedly, technique wobbles, or RPE creeps above 8.

Testing day setup and safety
- Separate lifts across two days (e.g., Mon lower + pull, Thu press + hinge). Keep total hard sets ≤10–12 per day.
- No HIIT that week; cardio easy only.
- Fuel well: pre-test 30–60 g carbs + 20–30 g protein; post-test 30–40 g protein + 60–80 g carbs.
- Sleep 8 h the night before; hydrate and include sodium if you sweat heavily.

When a true 1RM might be reasonable
- She has 6+ months consistent barbell experience with recent heavy singles exposure.
- No joint pain flags, sleep is solid, recovery metrics are good, and she’s not in a calorie deficit that week (eat at maintenance).
- Even then, cap at two lifts tested, use spotters/safeties, and stop one rep shy of a grind.

Bottom line
- Prefer submax 3–8RM tests and e1RM calculations in Week 12. If you really want to “see a single,” use a conservative RPE 8 heavy single with back-off work. This preserves the metabolic and hormonal priorities while giving you robust, trackable strength markers for the next block.
